html:
Aurangzeb was the sixth Mughal emperor, ruling from 1658 to 1707. Under him the empire reached its largest size, and the strains that broke it soon after his death set in.

He took the throne by force. When his father Shah Jahan fell ill in 1657, Aurangzeb beat his brothers, had his elder brother Dara Shikoh executed, and kept his father prisoner in Agra Fort.

He ruled as a strict Sunni Muslim. He had the great law code Fatawa-e-Alamgiri compiled, banned some court music and in 1679 brought back the jizya, a tax on non-Muslims that Akbar had dropped. He had the Sikh Guru Tegh Bahadur executed and pulled down some major temples. He also built the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore.

His last 26 years were spent in the Deccan. He took the sultanates of Bijapur in 1686 and Golconda in 1687, but he could not crush the Marathas that Shivaji had built up. The endless war drained the treasury. After he died at 88, his heirs fought one another and the Marathas spread north.
sum: Aurangzeb was the sixth Mughal emperor, ruling from 1658 to 1707. Under him the empire reached its largest size, and the strains that broke it soon after his death set in.
